400.t: Al Morgan, the bass player Hinton replaced in Cab Calloway's band
400.s: Hinton admires Al Morgan's elegance, and explains how Morgan left Calloway for Hollywood after being photographed in a film.
400.q: Al Morgan. He looked like he was almost seven foot tall. And immaculate. And always immaculate. And I was afraid to talk to him because he was just too great. But I’d stand, when his show was over I’d stand out by the curb and see how a bass player conducted himself. And he come out all sharply…

400.t: Three Deuces in Chicago and Zutty Singleton handing Hinton to Cab Calloway
400.s: Hinton, working at the Three Deuces with Zutty Singleton and Art Tatum, is looked over by Calloway, who asks Zutty for him; he calls his mother at 3 am.
400.q: Chu Berry. And they was always looking for a jam session. After they got through at the Grand Terrace they’d come down to the Three Deuces and jam with us. So Cab came down to the Three Deuces and saw the band down there, and he never said a word to me. He was all dressed up in a big cool tan coat…

400.t: Al Morgan, Charlie Carpenter and Cab Calloway's bass player idol
400.s: Hinton worshipped Al Morgan, Cab's bassist, outside the Regal, with the doorman Charlie Carpenter from his Boy Scout troop letting him in.
400.ch: Capone's Chicago, the union and hired by Cab
400.q: A little bit because in intermission we played pinochle and he put a big light behind him and he put the cards up like this. He put them all in place and he didn‟t look at them again. You just say ten of Jack, ten of spades and if he had the jack, he‟d put the jack on it. But I‟m working and Cab…

400.t: Cab Calloway asks Zutty for Hinton and the train to New York
400.s: Al Morgan quit Cab to stay in California; Keg Johnson recommended Hinton, and Cab came into the Three Deuces and got him released from Zutty.
400.ch: Capone's Chicago, the union and hired by Cab
400.q: So things got to be a little shaky there and one of the directors said to Al Morgan, “Look if you were out here in California every time we did a picture with a band you‟d have the job”, because he did his thing. So Al Morgan quit and stayed in California and joined Les Hiss‟ band with Lionel…

623.t: Ory's earlier band and Teddy Buckner joining
623.s: Musicians Smith heard with Ory in his college days, and the night Teddy Buckner first joined.
623.ch: Kid Ory band personnel and repertoire
623.q: Well, Buster Wilson was on the piano and Ed Garland, Montutti was with him in the minor hall and Bud Scott. I even heard Bud Scott. I don't think I ever heard Mutt Carey but I did hear people like Andrew Blakeney who I thought very highly of and I remember being in a club called the Beverly Cavern…

874.t: Cab Calloway, California, and the Les Hite band
874.s: Calloway's was his first big band; Milton Hinton replaced him. He stayed in California around 1934, then returned east in 1940 with Les Hite.
874.ch: New York and the swing years
874.q: Hinton, uh, no, yeah. After I left, Hinton took my place, because I was right here in California. See, I stayed out in California around 34. I didn't go back with Cab. I come out here with Cab a long time before. Then, then I went back east in 40, a little before the war, see. Yeah. And I went back…

62.t: Les Hite's band and bringing its trumpet section to Benny Carter
62.s: Prompted by a question about Gil Fuller, Wilson recalls joining Les Hite, Snooky arriving, a West Coast tour, and moving Hite's whole trumpet section to Benny Carter's band.
62.ch: Lunceford, Ellington, Gillespie and the big bands
62.q: Oh I know Gil, oh yeah I knew Gil real well yeah Gil was – he was with Les Hite’s band. See Dizzy and – and Gil Fuller played with Les Hite’s band. So when – when Les Hite came back to California, Dizzy and Gil Fuller didn’t come back, but they had a whole book full of Gil’s arrangements, and…

1.t: Keg Johnson, Al Morgan and how Milt got into Cab's band
1.s: Keg went to Cab; bassist Al Morgan quit Cab in California; and Keg then recommended Milt Hinton from Chicago.
1.ch: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
1.q: Well, maybe they got it today. Well, now I'm not involved with them youngsters. But I imagine it is. They know who is who, and who is on second first, and who is on and who ain't.

67.t: Joining Marion Hardy's Alabamians in Chicago
67.s: Back in New York he joined Hardy's Alabamians, working out of Chicago with Sonny Boy Williams, Eddie Mallory and Charlie Turner, until a Cotton Pickers offer came.
67.q: Yes. No, not in New York, they were at the Savoy, I went by to hear this band. Now that was a band -- there was a band who [had] -- yes, that's right, I went by the Savoy to hear this band. They had sent for me. Heard I was back.

70.t: Elton Hill, Eddie Mallory and Hardy's Alabamans
70.s: They discuss arranger Elton Hill, Eddie Mallory's band, and Marion Hardy's Alabamans, with whom Calloway first came to New York.
70.ch: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
70.q: Yes, I knew Elton Hill when he was with Tommy [Myles] in Washington and then later he was with Eddie Mallory at the same time --

7.t: How Milt Hinton came into Cab's band in Chicago
7.s: Hinton recalls Cab hearing him at the Three Deuces on Keg Johnson's recommendation after bassist Al Morgan stayed in California.
7.q: Well, that's when we come in town... We came in town that time with our best band.
